design: Regular/irregular subject plurals x subject number x attractor number in fronted prepositional frame. Attractor first, grammatical subject second. Compare to H586 with no refitting. Eight lexical quadruples per type/frame. Final token usually fixed. Subject-only and attractor-only Attention5 final-write swaps; full/zero, frozen ranks1/4/8, nuisance and five norm-matched random rank1 controls. No refitting.
hypotheses: Grammatical subject number: coefficient changes mainly with subject even under opposite attractor number.
Nearest-noun plurality: coefficient follows attractor at least as strongly.
Regular suffix proxy: effect weakens on irregular plurals.
Frame-dependent mixture: subject dominance in PP can fail in relative clauses.
gate: Per type/frame and per attractor number: >=4 subject pairs, >=75% both-endpoint candidate correctness, >=50% full-vocabulary intended-group top1. Retain every case.
scope: New prompt combinations, lexical overlap with earlier studies. Different token lengths possible and recorded; frame changes position and syntax together. Group NLL is not single-token CE.
